newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sandoz sells part of herbicide business.
newsitem.headline: Sandoz sells part of herbicide business.

text.p: Sandoz AG said it reached definitive agreement to sell a portion of its corn herbicide business to BASF AG for $695 million plus about $83 million in net working capital.

The sale includes substantially all rights to agricultural uses of Sandoz's corn herbicides in the United States and Canada, including the Banvel, Clarity and Marksman brands, the Frontier and Guardsman brands worldwide, and Sandoz Agro Inc's Beaumont, Texas manufacturing facility.
It said BASF has committed to offer jobs to a significant number of employees and the business is expected to generate $320 million in sales in 1996.
Sandoz said the sales is subject to regulatory approval, completion of the merger of Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy to form Novartis and other customary conditions.
It also said discussions continue with interested parties with respect to the previously announced sale of Sandoz's flea and tick product business in the United States and Canada.
The Sandoz/Ciba merger is on hold pending U.S. Federal Trade Commission approval.

When announcing first half results last month the companies said they were discussing with potential buyers divestment options in their U.S. crop protection and animal health businesses with the aim of expediting the FTC approval process.
The combined company would be a clear global leader in crop protection.

Novartis chief executive designate Daniel Vasella said in a recent interview with Reuters that the two companies were in the process of divesting their corn herbicide and their animal flea and tick control business in North America. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
